text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says 30 deputies from the conservative opposition are willing to join the government if MPs from the junior coalition partner quit.
- Businessmen's organisation propose new draft constitution to push democratisation.
- Islamic extremist sects threaten people who have unveiled their maltreatment of women and links to politicians.
- Oil giant Shell proposes working with Turkish state-owned pipeline company Botas to transport Qatari natural gas to Turkey.
- French politicians investigate allegations that police tortured young suspects in the town of Manisa last year.
- Thousands protest links between gangsters and the state in meetings held in Istanbul and Tarsus.
- Turkey's level of exports rise by 23 percent in the first half of January 1997 compared to the same period last year.
- State's package of financial help to the poor in southeastern Turkey is eaten up by high inflation. One can only buy 16 loaves of bread with the aid.
